claude.sample_unit: participants (623 lay people; 153 primary care physicians)

links.outcome: Whether users detect incorrect AI outputs / automation bias with LLM explanations, lay vs PCPs
links.effect: Lay users showed higher automation bias with LLM explanations (accuracy boosted when AI correct, reduced when AI erred); experienced PCPs remained resilient, benefiting irrespective of AI accuracy.
links.quote: However, LLM explanations yielded divergent effects: lay users showed higher automation bias – accuracy boosted when AI was correct, reduced when AI erred – while experienced PCPs remained resilient, benefiting irrespective of AI accuracy.

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance of clinicians and lay users when assisted by AI and XAI versus unassisted
links.effect: AI assistance balanced across skin tones improved accuracy and reduced diagnostic disparities; effects varied by explanation type, expertise, and timing.
links.quote: AI assistance balanced across skin tones improved accuracy and reduced diagnostic disparities.

unlisted_practices: Presenting AI suggestions after the user's initial independent assessment rather than first to reduce anchoring when AI is wrong

screen.practice: XAI explanations and AI suggestion timing (AI-first vs. clinician-first)
screen.reason: Empirical human-subjects experiment with laypeople and PCPs evaluating the impact of multimodal LLM explanations and timing of AI assistance on diagnostic performance and automation bias.

primary.practice: explainable AI and presentation timing of AI assistance
